resolutions.researcher_notes: Status is inferred by context, not a literal label (per protocol, this is expected for status refs). Searched both 'Jakhira'/'Intesar' and the alt spellings 'Jachira'/'Jakhara'/'Intisar'/'Idris' (concession 103) plus Arabic (الجاخرة) -- no dedicated news coverage of this specific small interconnector line exists; all hits trace to gem.wiki or to the unrelated, much larger 2024/2026 Intisar A/103-to-Brega trial-run pipeline (Libya Observer, Ecofin, Pipeline Technology Journal, PGJ -- a different, 42-in/~130km line, not this one). Direct opec.org PDF links are dead (301->homepage); the Wayback snapshot of OPEC ASB 2017 (Table 9.9, 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016') lists 'Jakhira/Intisar (2) | Wintershall | 2 x 50 [mi] | 8, 20 [in]' as a live, tabulated part of Libya's operating gas-pipeline network as of the 2016 data year (confirmed by direct pdftotext extraction of the PDF locally -- the verifier's PDF-binary substring check is a known false negative for this file type, per the script's own documented gotcha). Separately, a live (2024) Sarir Oil Operations tender for firefighting-system upgrades at the 'Jakhira station GOSP' confirms the Jakhira field/station is still an active, maintained facility as recently as 2024 -- consistent with, though not direct literal proof of, this specific gas line still operating today. No source suggests the line has been shut in or decommissioned.

OPEC ASB 2012 edition, Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011'), Libya section: 'Jakhira/Intesar | Wintershall | 80 [mi] | 20 [in] | 2,407,250 [1,000 scm/yr] | na'. Capacity column is in thousand standard cubic metres/year, so 2,407,250 x 1,000 scm/yr = 2.40725 bcm/y, matching GEM's recorded 2.40 bcm/y almost exactly (rounding). Confirmed by direct pdftotext extraction of the Wayback-hosted PDF (the live opec.org URL 301-redirects to the OPEC homepage and is dead). No other source located states a throughput/capacity figure for this specific line -- the 2017 ASB edition's equivalent table (9.9) has no Capacity column at all (diameter/length only), and no trade press or company page gives a capacity number for this small interconnector, so this stays single-source/tier=medium despite an extensive search (English + Arabic + alt spellings Jachira/Jakhara/Intisar/Idris/concession 103).

OPEC ASB 2017 edition, Table 9.9 ('Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016'), Libya section: 'Jakhira/Intisar (2) | Wintershall | 2 x 50 [mi] | 8, 20 [in]'. 2 x 50 miles = 100 miles = 160.9 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown=160.00 km closely (GEM appears to have summed both parallel pipes' lengths, per the source's own '(2)'/'2x' notation). Confirmed via direct pdftotext extraction of the Wayback snapshot (the live opec.org URL is dead, redirects to the homepage). VALUE-CONTRADICTION FLAG: the earlier OPEC ASB 2012 edition (Table 4.10, 2011 data year) shows this as a SINGLE 80-mile/20-inch line (128.7 km), with no second (8-in) pipe and no 160km total -- i.e. the second parallel pipe, and the combined 160km figure, only appear starting with the 2016 data year. Do not cite the 2012 edition for Length (it would show ~129km, not 160km); this is not a data error so much as the pipeline network having been expanded (a second, smaller-diameter line added) between the two data years.

Both OPEC ASB editions (2012 and 2017, Wayback) name the connection 'Jakhira/Intesar' / 'Jakhira/Intisar', matching GEM's Start/EndLocation. Independently (different origin from OPEC), Wintershall Dea's own newsroom confirms Jakhira (Area 91, ex-C96) is a real Sirte Basin field it operated -- via Wintershall Aktiengesellschaft (WIAG) -- until operatorship transferred to Sarir Oil Operations (a WIAG/NOC joint venture) on 29 October 2020; a separately located, independent pumpsandsystems.com trade article (2015) also describes 'a gas processing plant at the Jakhira site' in the Sirte Basin desert, further corroborating the start point. Intesar/Intisar is a separate, large, well-documented Sirte Basin field (Occidental discovery, 1967; part of the Zueitina Oil Co. concession per USGS Minerals Yearbook 2016, distinct from Wintershall's own concession) -- corroborated across OPEC ASB, USGS, and Wood Mackenzie field reports, all independent of GEM. CAVEAT: StartState/Province and EndState/Province are both recorded as 'Sirte Basin', a geological/informal region rather than a Libyan administrative province (Jakhira sits in the Al Wahat district per Wintershall Dea's own description) -- a minor precision issue, not a contradiction, and consistent with how sibling rows in this batch are recorded.

GEM records Owner1='BASF' 100% with no ref. Both OPEC ASB editions (2012 Table 4.10, 2017 Table 9.9) name the pipeline's owner/operator column simply 'Wintershall', never 'BASF'. An independent 2015 pumpsandsystems.com trade article states plainly that 'Wintershall' is 'a BASF subsidiary' operating the Jakhira gas processing plant -- this is the source that most directly supports the GEM value as a defensible parent-company simplification (Wintershall Aktiengesellschaft/Wintershall Holding GmbH was a wholly BASF-owned entity before the 2019 DEA merger created the jointly-owned Wintershall Dea). VALUE-CONTRADICTION FLAG (do not silently overwrite -- flag only): (1) USGS Minerals Yearbook 2016 (Table 2, Libya) lists the Jakhira/As-Sarah/Nakhla/Tauma concession itself as a 'Wintershall joint venture [National Oil Corp. (NOC), 51%, and Wintershall Holding GmbH, 49%]' -- i.e. at the concession/equity level Wintershall Holding GmbH held only a 49% interest, not 100%, so 'BASF 100%' is at best a simplification collapsing two different corporate layers (BASF's ownership of the Wintershall entity vs. Wintershall's minority equity share of the actual Libyan concession JV). (2) Wintershall Dea's own newsroom (verified, independent of OPEC) confirms operatorship of these exact Sirte Basin fields (Jakhira/As-Sarah, Area 91) was transferred on 29 October 2020 from WIAG to Sarir Oil Operations (SOO), a new joint venture between WIAG and Libya's NOC -- meaning even 'Wintershall' alone is now a stale operator/owner attribution; SOO (the WIAG/NOC JV) is the more current entity. Recommend flagging Owner1='BASF' as an Update-candidate correction (Wintershall / Sarir Oil Operations JV), not applying it here -- staging only, per protocol.
